SQL:
WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "customers.tier",
    COUNT(*) AS "customers.n_customers",
    COUNT(DISTINCT customers.id) AS "customers.n_distinct"
  FROM customers AS customers
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
), _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum AS (
  SELECT
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.amount_sum"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  GROUP BY
    customers.tier
)
SELECT
  _base."customers.tier",
  _base."customers.n_customers",
  _base."customers.n_distinct",
  _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.amount_sum" AS "customers.revenue"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum
  ON _base."customers.tier" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_customers__orders__amount_sum."orders.customers.tier"
ORDER BY
  _base."customers.tier" ASC
LIMIT 21

args.message: Customer counts include every customer in each tier, even those with no orders (bronze 100, gold 43, silver 59). Revenue is the sum of order amounts for each tier, calculated separately from the customer count so the join to orders doesn't inflate either number. Customers with no orders add nothing to revenue.
